title: Variance-optimal release raised half-loss probability in 520 of 2991 selected mouse contact models
abstract: We tested whether variance-optimal release also lowers large-response-loss probability. Independent Bernoulli events, exact local mean compensation and a mean event probability of 0.5 were assumed. Exact event sums used 1519 Allen V1DD and 1472 MICrONS connections. Inclusive half-mean loss probability increased in 258 and 262 connections, despite lower variance. Mean loss probability fell from 0.231537 to 0.115702 and from 0.232716 to 0.106582. Exact threshold ties explain many adverse cases. A strict half threshold still left 33 and 38 adverse cases. At threshold 0.75, mean loss probability increased in both maps. Full enumeration and count convolution agreed within 1.12e-15. A synthetic example separates variance, silence and half-loss. Exact compensation, assumed rates, uncertain size proxies, partial arbors and one mouse per map limit biological use. No release or activity data were measured. Code, aggregate evidence, figure, hashes and external regeneration steps support reproduction; contact records are excluded.

display.caption: Variance-optimal minus uniform loss probability at five thresholds and across selected connections. Independent release, exact mean compensation and b=0.5 are assumed.
